title: Why do planets go round the Sun?
examples: Does the Sun pull the planets with a rope?
What keeps the Earth from flying away from the Sun?
Is it like a giant spinning merry-go-round?

explain.say: The Sun has a special pull called gravity. Gravity pulls things with mass towards each other.

draw.text: Why do planets go round the Sun?

explain.say: Gravity is like an invisible rope pulling everything towards the Sun. Bigger things have stronger gravity.
The planets also have their own speed. They want to keep moving in a straight line always.
So, the Sun's gravity pulls them, but their own speed keeps them moving sideways. This makes them circle.
When you swing a ball on a string, the string pulls it, but your arm keeps it moving around you.

draw.text: Swinging a ball on a string.

explain.say: A real life example is a ball on a string. The string pulls it, but you swing it fast enough to make it circle.

draw.text: Swinging a ball in a circle.

faq.q: Does the Sun pull the planets with a rope?
faq.a: No, it is not like a real rope. Gravity is an invisible force that pulls things together.
asks: Does the Sun use a string to pull us?

faq.q: Why don't the planets just fall into the Sun?
faq.a: They are moving sideways very fast. This sideways push keeps them from falling straight in.
asks: If gravity pulls, why don't they crash?
What stops them from falling in?

faq.q: Is the pull the same for all planets?
faq.a: No, the pull is stronger for bigger things. The Sun is much bigger than any planet.
asks: Does Jupiter feel the pull more than Earth?
Is the pull stronger close to the Sun?

faq.q: Does the Earth pull the Sun?
faq.a: No, the Sun is much bigger and has much more gravity. The Sun's pull is much stronger.

faq.q: Is orbiting the same as spinning?
faq.a: Spinning is going around an axis, like a top. Orbiting is going around another big object, like the Sun.
asks: What is the difference between spinning and orbiting?
Can something spin and orbit at the same time?

facts: Gravity is the force that pulls objects with mass together.
Planets orbit the Sun because of gravity and their forward speed.
The Sun has the strongest gravity in our solar system.
The faster a planet moves, the wider its orbit tends to be.

quiz.say: What is the main force pulling planets toward the Sun?
quiz.why: Gravity is the invisible pull between objects with mass.

wrong.0: While magnetic forces exist, gravity is the main pull here.
wrong.2: Speed is the sideways push, not the pull.
wrong.3: Planets are not connected by physical ropes.

quiz.say: If a planet stopped moving sideways, what would happen?

options.show: It would fall into the Sun.
options.say: It would fall into the Sun.

quiz.why: Without sideways speed, gravity would pull it straight in.

wrong.0: Floating away needs no pull, but gravity is always pulling.
wrong.1: Staying in place means no movement at all.
wrong.2: Speed and falling are different things.

quiz.say: What combination keeps planets in orbit?
quiz.why: Both the pull and the push are needed for a stable circle.

wrong.0: Light is energy, not the force that pulls.
wrong.2: Only gravity would make the planet fall in.
wrong.3: Only speed would make the planet fly away.
